**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

there's a lot of tests for pickling w/ options, OK, good test case lets see what it is

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

First observation, i get your stack trace on python 2, on python 3 I get:


```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "test.py", line 98, in <module>
    pickle.dumps(garply_again)
_pickle.PicklingError: Can't pickle <function datetime.now at 0x7f73432c51e0>: attribute lookup datetime.now on __main__ failed

```

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

next observation, this is local to subqueryload()

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

mmm nope, im wrong on that, let's try more carefully

**Nick Pilon ([@npilon](https://github.com/npilon)) wrote:**

I got both the datetime.now error and the weakref error from our code when trying different work-arounds. I should also have noted that setting `propagate_to_loaders = False` on the `subqueryload` does avoid the problem.

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

OK so i think this isn't actually "new".   1.2 improves the loader options and in 1.1 it seems your BarBaz object isn't getting carried along in the options for the objects in Garply.foos.  I can't pickle the BarBaz object in 1.1 either.

**Nick Pilon ([@npilon](https://github.com/npilon)) wrote:**

I wasn't sure if the BarBaz object is supposed to be pickle-able or not.

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

OK the AliasedClass was never directly pickle-able without using the "serializer" extension: http://docs.sqlalchemy.org/en/latest/core/serializer.html   (don't use that).   So let's see if the BarBaz object is not supposed to be in the options for the related objects...because I'm not sure why they'd need to be there.

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

oh, no, those are supposed to be there.   this is not looking good.   im not sure why in 1.1 your of_type() is totally blown away from the options.

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

alright.  in 1.1 the of_type is stored differently and is just lost in the pickle.    given the object w/ the load_options:


```
1.1

(Pdb) !list(g.foos[0]._sa_instance_state.load_options)[0].__getstate__()
{'_is_chain_link': False, 'local_opts': {}, 'path': [(<class '__main__.Garply'>, 'foos')], 'propagate_to_loaders': True, '_to_bind': set([<sqlalchemy.orm.strategy_options._UnboundLoad object at 0x7f0736861b90>]), 'strategy': (('lazy', 'joined'),)}


1.2

!list(g.foos[0]._sa_instance_state.load_options)[0].__getstate__()
{'_is_chain_link': False, 'local_opts': {}, 'is_class_strategy': False, 'path': [(<class '__main__.Garply'>, 'foos', <AliasedClass at 0x7feb2ad58550; Foo>)], 'propagate_to_loaders': True, '_to_bind': [<sqlalchemy.orm.strategy_options._UnboundLoad object at 0x7feb2b5d94d0>], 'strategy': (('lazy', 'joined'),)}

```

now, what if the path is more tokens than that.   what does 1.1 do?  stay tuned.

OK, adding another link in the chain, does of_type still get lost?

```
q = Session.query(Garply).options(
    joinedload(Garply.foos.of_type(BarBaz)).joinedload(BarBaz.hohos)
)

```

then we see the option in 1.1:


```
!list(g.foos[0]._sa_instance_state.load_options)[0].__getstate__()
{'_is_chain_link': False, 'local_opts': {}, 'path': [(<class '__main__.Garply'>, 'foos'), (<class '__main__.Foo'>, 'hohos')], 'propagate_to_loaders': True, '_to_bind': set([<sqlalchemy.orm.strategy_options._UnboundLoad object at 0x7f2140a96b10>, <sqlalchemy.orm.strategy_options._UnboundLoad object at 0x7f2140a96a50>]), 'strategy': (('lazy', 'joined'),)}

```

of_type is just gone.   So.....we can likely make 1.2 do that in pickling, just lose the of_type part since that's usually where an AliasedClass is hiding.

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

surprise.   there's a flag that does exactly this which I added within the scope of 1.2, and I am not using anywhere :).    guess I meant to use it here :)

```
diff --git a/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/strategy_options.py b/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/strategy_options.py
index de9a11c56..5738069ab 100644
--- a/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/strategy_options.py
+++ b/lib/sqlalchemy/orm/strategy_options.py
@@ -439,7 +439,7 @@ class _UnboundLoad(Load):
 
     def __getstate__(self):
         d = self.__dict__.copy()
-        d['path'] = self._serialize_path(self.path)
+        d['path'] = self._serialize_path(self.path, reject_aliased_class=True)
         return d
 
     def __setstate__(self, state):

```

**Nick Pilon ([@npilon](https://github.com/npilon)) wrote:**

For my use case, at least, I don't care about these options getting lost in the pickle. The entire reason we have them is so that we can use the unpickled objects without needing a database.

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

ok needs some more than that

**Michael Bayer ([@zzzeek](https://github.com/zzzeek)) wrote:**

Don't include AliasedClass when pickling options

Fixed 1.2 regression where a mapper option that contains an
:class:`.AliasedClass` object, as is typical when using the
:meth:`.QueryableAttribute.of_type` method, could not be pickled.   1.1's
behavior was to omit the aliased class objects from the path, so this
behavior is restored.

Change-Id: I4b36a422b7c0e6a6da7ee3ba3ab282c13917a31f
Fixes: #4209


→ 08a8e8cf3b06
